Fashion experts have predicted Taylor Swift will wear four dresses during her wedding to Travis Kelce.

The pop superstar, 36, is expected to marry the NFL player at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Friday (04.07.26) and the fashion industry is buzzing with excitement about the singer's choice of wedding dress designer - with some suggesting Taylor will opt for several costume changes during her big day to cover "multiple silhouettes".

Kelly Cook, CEO of David's Bridal, told WWD: "We think she's going to be into multiple outfit changes. That's going to be potentially everything from the entrance dress to the ceremony dress, the reception dress and the exit dress.

"We're expecting multiple silhouettes - short and skimpy, romantic and old Hollywood glamour."

Bridal designer and retailer Mark Ingram told the publication Taylor may choose just two looks - one "huge and grand" dress for the ceremony and a shorter style for the reception, adding: "It's going to be a feast for the eyes. There are all kinds of bets on what she's going to wear ...

"This is really going to cause some excitement in the industry."

WWD reports there are rumours suggesting Taylor may have chosen to have her dress designed by Sarah Burton, the designer who created the gown worn by Catherine, Princess of Wales at her wedding to Prince William back in 2011.

Burton was working at Alexander McQueen when she created the dress for Catherine, but she has since moved to Givenchy where she is creative director.

The publication states Taylor may have dropped a big hint about her fashion choices on her big day when she wore a Givenchy gown when she was inducted to the Songwriters Hall of Fame on June 11 - just weeks before her rumoured wedding date.

However, other sources suggest Taylor may opt for a gown designed by Jonathan Anderson of Christian Dior.

The Hollywood Reporter states: "Well-placed sources say the winning dress - the dress that will likely transition Taylor Swift to Mrs. Travis Kelce - is a custom couture gown by Jonathan Anderson of Christian Dior ...

"Now, might Swift switch it up and tie the knot in one of her many other bridal event looks? Sure. But if you’ve got a Jonathan Anderson Dior couture gown, why would you?"
